title: Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
requirement: Landlords may terminate a tenancy only for the ordinance's just causes and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions; since March 27, 2023, a tenant may not be evicted for non-payment unless the arrears exceed the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO; tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first.

conditions.text: Units already regulated by the City's Rent Stabilization Ordinance

applicability.per_tenancy: Tenant has lived in the same unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first.
coverage_quotes: The JCO covers most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles that are not regulated by the City’s Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).
In order to apply to a tenancy, it requires that the tenant either has lived in the same unit for at least six months or that their original lease expired, whichever comes first.

exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless or short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and some properties owned by HACLA or the government.
citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §165.00 et seq.)
quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
interaction: Does not regulate rent increases; state law AB 1482 may regulate rent amounts in buildings older than 15 years.

title: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) annual rent cap
requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 the maximum allowable increase is 8.9%.
coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years; units built within the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable units, a two-unit owner-occupied property, certain dormitories, qualifying single-family homes and condominiums, and units under the City's RSO are exempt.
